songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line
Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Pigpen fronted set with monster Good Lovin' & epic Bird Song
ai_show_review.blurb: The Princeton show bursts with Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals and a legendary 27‑minute Good Lovin' that includes his famous Brooklyn Bridge rap. Highlights also include an extended Bird Song suite (Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad → Turn On Your Lovelight) and tight, driving performances of Truckin', Hard To Handle, and Casey Jones. Soundboard recordings capture the band in crisp, high‑fidelity form.
ai_show_review.review: April 17, 1971 at Dillon Gym finds the Dead riding a wave of pure, unfiltered energy. From the opening riff of Truckin' straight through to a rousing Big Boss Man, the first set stays solid and danceable, but it’s the second set that truly shines. A monster Good Lovin'—spanning nearly half an hour—features Pigpen’s iconic Brooklyn Bridge rap, his searing harmonica, and a rhythm section locked in by Bill Kreutzmann’s driving drums and Phil Lesh’s propulsive bass. The jam segues into a soaring Bird Song suite (Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad → Turn On Your Lovelight) that feels both exploratory and cohesive, showcasing Jerry Garcia’s expressive lead work and the band’s collective chemistry. With pristine soundboard clarity, this performance stands as one of the most vivid snapshots of Pigpen‑fronted magic in the early ’70s.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with excellent clarity; highlights Pigpen’s vocals and the epic Good Lovin' jam without any audible flaws.

key_highlights: Explosive Good Lovin' featuring Pigpen’s legendary Brooklyn Bridge rap
Epic Bird Song suite (Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad → Turn On Your Lovelight) delivers a soaring jam
Tight, high‑energy renditions of Truckin', Hard To Handle and Casey Jones
Crystal‑clear soundboard recording preserves every nuance of the performance

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is tight and expressive throughout, adding extra flair on “Beat It On Down the Line” and delivering a soaring solo during the Good Lovin' jam.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a thunderous, supportive bass line that anchors the extended improvisations, especially evident in the Bird Song suite.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocals are solid on tracks like “Mama Tried” and “Casey Jones,” and his rhythm guitar locks in tightly with the band’s groove.
band_performance.Pigpen: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan is in top form, delivering powerhouse vocals, gritty harmonica, and the famed Brooklyn Bridge rap that defines this Good Lovin' performance.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann drives the band with hot, pocket‑perfect drumming, laying a solid foundation for both the high‑energy rockers and the sprawling jams.
